title: Put political appointees in charge of HUD offices
proposal: The chapter says HUD leaders should give all delegated powers to political appointees, convert career leadership jobs into political positions, and use Senior Executive Service transfers to install aligned leaders.
quote: change any current career leadership positions into political and non-career appointment positions; and use Senior Executive Service (SES) transfers to install motivated and aligned leadership.

title: Add the HUD Secretary to the foreign investment review committee
proposal: The chapter says the President should issue an executive order making the HUD Secretary a member of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the U.S., to watch foreign (especially Chinese) ownership of U.S. housing.
quote: The President should issue an executive order making the HUD Secretary a member of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the U.S.

title: Create a task force to reverse Biden-era HUD actions
proposal: The chapter says the HUD Secretary should set up a task force of political appointees to find and reverse all Biden Administration actions that it says advanced progressive ideology.
quote: The Secretary should initiate a HUD task force consisting of politically appointed personnel to identify and reverse all actions taken by the Biden Administration

title: Review HUD guidance issued outside formal rulemaking
proposal: The chapter says HUD leaders should thoroughly review all guidance documents that were issued without going through the Administrative Procedure Act process.
quote: should conduct a thorough review of all subregulatory guidance that has been instituted outside of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
agency: HUD / Office of the Secretary, OGC

title: End the PAVE home appraisal equity policies
proposal: The chapter says HUD should immediately end the Biden Administration's Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity (PAVE) policies and reverse related actions on home appraisals.
quote: Immediately end the Biden Administration’s Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity (PAVE) policies

title: Repeal HUD climate change initiatives and spending
proposal: The chapter says HUD should repeal climate change initiatives and spending in its budget request.
quote: Repeal climate change initiatives and spending in the department’s budget request.

title: Repeal the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing rule
proposal: The chapter says HUD should repeal the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) regulation brought back under the Biden Administration, and stop using special-purpose credit authority to further equity.
quote: Repeal the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) regulation reinstituted under the Biden Administration30 and any other uses of special-purpose credit authorities to further equity.

title: Eliminate the Housing Supply Fund
proposal: The chapter says HUD should eliminate the new Housing Supply Fund.
quote: any other uses of special-purpose credit authorities to further equity.31 4. Eliminate the new Housing Supply Fund.

title: Bar noncitizens and mixed-status families from federal housing aid
proposal: The chapter says HUD should restart a Trump-era proposed rule that would prohibit noncitizens, including families with mixed immigration status, from living in any federally assisted housing.
quote: The Office of the Secretary should recommence proposed regulation put forward under the Trump Administration that would prohibit noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from living in all federally assisted housing.

title: Add work requirements and time limits to HUD rental aid
proposal: The chapter says HUD should strengthen work requirements and set maximum time limits for residents in project-based and tenant-based rental assistance, through rules and new laws.
quote: strengthen work and work-readiness requirements,35 implement maximum term limits for residents in PBRA and TBRA programs

title: Reduce marriage penalties in housing assistance
proposal: The chapter says HUD should reduce what it calls the anti-marriage bias in housing aid, and Congress should remove benefit rules that discourage work and marriage.
quote: HUD should implement reforms reducing the implicit anti-marriage bias in housing assistance programs

title: End "Housing First" homelessness policies
proposal: The chapter says HUD should end Housing First policies and instead focus on mental health and substance abuse, shifting toward transitional housing.
quote: and end Housing First37 policies so that the department prioritizes mental health and substance abuse issues before jumping to permanent interventions in homelessness.

title: Suspend HUD outside research grants
proposal: The chapter says HUD's research office should suspend all outside research and evaluation grants and end or move functions not related to data collection, surveys or regulatory analysis.
quote: should suspend all external research and evaluation grants in the Office of Policy Development and Research

title: Raise FHA insurance premiums on longer mortgages
proposal: The chapter says FHA should raise mortgage insurance premiums for all loans longer than 20 years and keep premiums the same for shorter loans and refinances.
quote: FHA leadership should increase the mortgage insurance premium (MIP) for all products above 20-year terms and maintain MIP for all products below 20-year terms

title: Overhaul FHA reverse mortgages, loan limits and short-term loans
proposal: The chapter says Congress should consider moving the reverse mortgage (HECM) program to its own insurance fund, revising loan limits, and allowing shorter-term loans that pay down principal faster.
quote: Moving the Home Equity Conversion Mortgages (HECM) program once again to its own special risk insurance fund.

title: Limit FHA mortgage insurance to first-time buyers
proposal: The chapter says FHA single-family mortgage insurance should be restricted by law to first-time homebuyers, and federal "affirmative obligation" authorities for single-family programs should be dropped.
quote: Statutorily restricting eligibility for first-time homebuyers and abandoning the affirmative obligation authorities erected for the single-family housing programs

title: Move HUD's inspection center to the Office of Housing
proposal: The chapter says the HUD Secretary should move the Real Estate Assessment Center from Public and Indian Housing to the Office of Housing, and consider private accreditation for inspections.
quote: The HUD Secretary should move the HUD Real Estate Assessment Center (REAC) from PIH to the Office of Housing

title: Keep HUD technology modernization funding
proposal: The chapter says HUD should keep its requested budget for technology modernization projects.
quote: HUD should maintain its requested budget authority for modernization initiatives that are applicable to the Office of the Chief Information Officer

title: Oppose federal efforts to weaken single-family zoning
proposal: The chapter says localities, not the federal government, should decide zoning, and the Administration should oppose efforts to weaken single-family zoning or have federal law override local land use decisions.
quote: Localities rather than the federal government must have the final say in zoning laws and regulations, and a conservative Administration should oppose any efforts to weaken single-family zoning.

title: Tax credits to repair rural housing
proposal: The chapter says Congress could propose tax credits for renovating or repairing housing in rural areas.
quote: Congress can propose tax credits for the renovation or repair of housing stock in rural areas

title: Favor housing vouchers and let public housing land be sold
proposal: The chapter says new laws should favor housing vouchers over site-based subsidies and give public housing agencies maximum flexibility to sell public housing land.
quote: provide authority for maximal flexibility to direct PHA land sales that involve the existing stock of public housing units.

title: Consider breaking up HUD and shifting its work to states
proposal: The chapter says Congress could consider a full overhaul of HUD that hands many functions to states and localities and moves the rest to other agencies, such as loan guarantees to SBA and Indian housing to Interior.
quote: Congress could consider a wholesale overhaul of HUD that contemplates devolving many HUD functions to states and localities
